_comment: compose/types_manifest.py. Mirrors the symbol analyzer's seed + closure model.
PORT-SCOPE types (defined_in is a file in <target>/crustify/scope.json) are the
porting subjects - they carry the full declared-field layout and are rewritten
as native Rust types. WRAP-SCOPE types (reached by port code) carry the base
schema with fields[] narrowed to the port-accessed subset (the FFI surface).
Every struct (port and wrap) also carries the opaque_in + non_opaque_in consumer
footprints. Records below illustrate port and wrap structs and an enum. (Callbacks
and other function-pointer typedefs are SYMBOLS - emitted into syms.json, not here.)
_comment_type: type - the C struct/union/enum tag, or the synthetic name for a string / array
_comment_typedef: typedef - list of typedef aliases that resolve to this tag (e.g. SSL_SESSION for
ssl_session_st). Composer-filled; [] when there is none.
_comment_kind: kind - Composer-emitted: struct, union (its own kind - same member-layout
skeleton as a struct, but NOT analyzed: the type-analyzer worklist is
structs-only, so a union's lifecycle/accessor slots stay at skeleton
defaults), enum. (Function-pointer typedefs are kind:"callback" SYMBOLS in
syms.json, not types.) Agent-synthesized: string (a NUL-string allocator/free/
(a sized-buffer allocator/free/ops cluster), both made by the buffer pass. A
generated-container instance (a struct produced by a DEFINE_*/setup macro) is
NOT a distinct kind - it stays kind:"struct" and is analyzed as an ordinary
struct. The kind axis is orthogonal to port/wrap scope - port types are
overwhelmingly struct/enum; the synthetic kinds are almost always wrap-scope
_comment_declared_in: declared_in - LIST of repo-root-relative header paths that declare the type
(always a JSON array, even for a single header). Same shape as the syms base.
Composer-filled for composer-emitted types; agent-synthesized kinds (string /
array) must emit it as a list too - never a bare string.
_comment_defined_in: defined_in - repo-root-relative path to the file holding the definition;
nullable. Composer-filled. Port-vs-wrap scope is NOT a manifest field - the
orchestrator computes it (defined_in in scope.json) and passes it to the analyzer
as a prompt arg per entry.
_comment_ops: ops - ONLY on the synthetic string/array clusters (kind string/array), which
are fieldless: their explicit method list (alloc/realloc/free/cleanse). A
CONCRETE type (struct/union/enum) has NO `ops` field - its method surface is
DERIVED and is its lifecycle ONLY (ctors/dtor/up_ref/clones/locking). Field
accessors are NOT part of it: the wrapper derives per-field accessors from the
field layout directly, so a C field-accessor function is an ordinary free
function. A function that is not a lifecycle routine belongs to no type - it
stays a free function, visible only in the opaque_in/non_opaque_in footprints.
_comment_array_fields: elems / len_aware_drop - ARRAY-only (a string is a single buffer and carries
neither; its clearing release is just its dtor's single releaser (exclusive or
shared)). `elems` lists the concrete element types the buffer holds at call
sites - rows {type, note} - which become the array wrapper's typed CVec<T>
aliases. `len_aware_drop` is true when the C release takes (ptr, len) and zeroes
that region (clearing / *_clear_free), so the CVec strategy's cleanup forwards
with the right signature. Whether a ported array DROPS its elements (ownership)
is NOT here - it is a PORT concern, captured per-field as ptr.owned_elem.
_comment_ctors: ctors - agent-filled: the function(s) that produce a fresh T from raw inputs. A
function MAY appear in BOTH ctors[] and up_ref when it allocates a fresh T on one
control path and increments an existing T's refcount on another (cache-aware
open: e.g. git_mwindow_get_pack allocates on cache miss, atomic-incs on hit).
_comment_up_ref: up_ref - agent-filled refcount-increment op, or null. May coexist with ctors
_comment_dtor: dtor - agent-filled {shared, exclusive, fields}: the destructor roles
(load-bearing for Rust Drop and the CBox / CVal / CArc routing). `exclusive` is
a plain *_free releasing a SOLELY-owned heap header AND its owned fields -> CBox
/ CFreed. `shared` is a REFCOUNT-DECREMENTING free (the dual-ownership /
refcounted teardown; pairs with `up_ref` being set) -> CArc / CRefCounted.
`fields` is a *_dispose / *_cleanup releasing owned fields ONLY, leaving the
by-value header for the caller/parent -> CVal / CValued. A single C function may
fill AT MOST ONE role (the three MUST name different functions); a type with a
plain free and a separate disposer sets two roles. All three null -> POD value,
no teardown. (Legacy {storage, fields} manifests are tolerated during migration:
`storage` maps to `shared` when `up_ref` is set, else to `exclusive`; see
_comment_clones: clones - agent-filled LIST of deep-copy ops (e.g. SSL_dup), [] if none. A
list because one type may expose several (a plain deep-copy plus a
_comment_locking: locking - agent-filled {acquire, release, locks, locked_fields}, or null.
_comment_conditional_drop: conditional_drop - agent-filled {skip_when, skip_when_kind}, or null. Names a gate
a hypothetical Rust Drop on T must honor BUT that the dtor function itself doesn't
encode. A dtor whose prologue already checks the condition (e.g. if (--p->refcount
> 0) return;) keeps conditional_drop:null - Rust Drop calling the C dtor
short-circuits naturally. A dtor that unconditionally releases storage while a
sibling release function does the gating (refcount-dec in git_mwindow_put_pack ->
git_packfile_free) fills it so Rust can port the gate into its impl. Plain
NULL-on-entry guards (if (!p) return;) are NOT conditional_drop.
_comment_casted: casted - {to: [tags], from: [tags]}, composer-filled from the raw
type is cast INTO (it is a cast operand); `from` = tags cast INTO this
type (it is a cast result). Both are canonical struct tags (typedef
spellings resolved), [] when none. STORED RAW AND UNCLASSIFIED: the same
relation surfaces several C idioms - generated-container erasure (an instance
casts to its type-erased engine, e.g. stack_st_X509 -> stack_st, with the
reverse from value getters); embedded-base DOWNCAST (a base handle cast to a
wider type, e.g. ssl_st -> ssl_connection_st; the UPCAST is &wider->base field
arithmetic, NOT a cast, so it is absent); ASN1 ITEM punning (x509_st <->
ASN1_VALUE_st). Consumers disambiguate by field shape / cast in-degree /
first-member embedding; nothing is baked in here. An erasure engine is
recognizable as a high-`from`-in-degree cast target of a name-family of
_comment_opaque_in: opaque_in - composer-filled {file: [symbols]} footprint: functions that touch
this type but only as an OPAQUE HANDLE, never accessing a field (forwarders,
allocate-and-return ctors, delegating wrappers like SSL_SESSION_dup -> dup_intern).
The agent reads it for lifecycle/forwarder op candidates. ALL STRUCTS carry it.
COMPLETE / scope-agnostic for every type (port AND wrap): every consumer
tree-wide is listed. The per-target scope view is applied at READ time by
_comment_non_opaque_in: read/write a FIELD of this type and so need its concrete layout (incl. transitive
a->b->field reachers). Strong op signal for the agent. ALL STRUCTS carry it.
COMPLETE / scope-agnostic like opaque_in: the FULL cross-codebase footprint for
every type - required for ABI/layout completeness and to retain out-of-scope
lifecycle ops (a wrap-side up_ref/dup) the Rust port honors. `query` applies the
per-target scope view at read time (--port-only/--wrap-only).
_comment_fields: fields - per-field records. Scalar single -> {name} (layout-agnostic; bindgen
handles it). Scalar array / by-value aggregate / aggregate array ->
{name, type, ref:"value", array?}. Pointer (single or array) ->
{name, type, ref:"pointer", ptr:{...}, array?}. type is the element type (full,
including *), omitted for scalar singles. ref is value/pointer (the element's
reference kind), omitted for scalar singles. array is {size:N} (fixed) /
{size:null} (flexible/incomplete member), omitted when not an array.
Port-scope types list ALL declared fields (full layout); wrap-scope types list
only the port-accessed subset. Anonymous-aggregate-typed fields carry the raw
(unnamed ...) type string; deep nested inlining is deferred - see docs/TODOS.md Sec anon.
_comment_ptr: ptr - per pointer field (and per element of a pointer array). Composer emits a
null skeleton; the agent fills it, folded into the lifecycle pass. Fields: array
(pointee is a buffer - companion length field), string (pointee is a
NUL-terminated string; mutually exclusive with array), owned (the struct owns
the pointee, freed in the type's dtor - the moved analog), exclusive (only when
owned: sole ownership -> Box/CBox), shared (only when owned, mutually exclusive
with exclusive: the pointee is refcounted/shared -> Arc/CArc, the pointee type
has up_ref; mirrors the pointee type's dtor.shared and may be composer-derived
from it), borrowed (non-owning reference; mutually exclusive with owned),
nullable (can be NULL -> Rust Option<...>), mutable (3-state null/true/false;
const-in-type -> false; pointer-to-user-defined-type -> null;
buffers/out-scalars -> agent decides), lifetime (when borrowed: self = bounded
by the enclosing struct; field:<name> = points into a sibling field's storage;
static = global; other = escape hatch with note), container (this pointer holds
a collection of element pointers - e.g. a stack/map backing array - vs a single
pointee), owned_elem (only when container=true: does the struct own and free the
ELEMENTS, or merely borrow them?), note (free-form). Invariants:
ownedXORborrowed; exclusive only when owned; exclusive XOR shared when owned;
owned_elem only when container; borrowed=>lifetime set; stringXORarray;
const=>mutable=false. Ownership analysis applies to BOTH port and wrap pointer
fields - for wrap fields it also drives accessor generation (interior-mutability
getters): mutable decides whether the wrap struct needs a field_mut() getter;
owned/borrowed decide whether the getter returns an owning wrapper or a borrowed
handle; nullable/array/string decide the return shape (Option / slice / CStr
view).

layout + GLOBAL opaque_in/non_opaque_in footprints (port types keep the
cross-codebase footprint). Method surface = lifecycle ONLY (no `ops`);
field accessors are derived from the layout, not stored. A pointer field

ptr.note: Session-secret buffer; allocated in statem_secret_new, zeroed + freed in statem_secret_free.

_comment_example: Wrap-scope struct (defined outside scope.json) reached by port code.
Footprints are COMPLETE (scope-agnostic): every consumer tree-wide appears,
so out-of-scope lifecycle (SSL_SESSION_up_ref / SSL_SESSION_dup) is visible
via `query --methods` and gets filled here. `query` applies the per-target
scope view at read time (--port-only/--wrap-only). Fields carry their
structural shape (type/ref/array); pointer fields also get a ptr block.

ptr.note: Peer cert; refcounted (X509_up_ref / X509_free). mutable=null: opaque-handle field, accessor returns a borrowed handle.
